column1: # Hand-written tips on playing Elite Dangerous, one per row: key, the journal event that triggers it, the tip.
# The Narrator rewords a tip as narration and invents none. Rows are tried in file order.

column3: tip
A ship with a fuel scoop fitted refuels for free by flying close to the corona of a star of spectral class O, B, A, F, G, K or M.
Firing the discovery scanner after a jump reveals the bodies in the system, which can then be scanned for a closer look.
Scooping fuel heats the ship, and heat past the limit damages modules, so the heat gauge is worth watching and the ship should pull away from the star if it climbs.
A route plotted in the galaxy map targets each system in turn, so the ship can jump along it by charging the frame shift drive once the next system is selected.
As a destination nears in supercruise, the throttle should come back into the blue zone so the ship can drop out beside the target instead of overshooting it.
Close to a station the ship is mass locked and cannot engage supercruise, so it should fly clear of the station before charging the frame shift drive.
A docking clearance gives a landing pad and a time limit, and the clearance lapses if the ship does not reach the pad in time.
The outfitting screen at a station lets the ship buy, sell and change its modules.
The services a station offers, such as a market, mission board, shipyard, outfitting and repairs, differ from station to station.
A station with a repair service mends the hull and modules for a fee, so a damaged ship can be made whole again at dock.
Insurance replaces a destroyed ship for its rebuy cost, a fraction of the ship's value, so a pilot should keep that much in credits before a risky flight.
Scan data is worth credits at the Universal Cartographics service of a station, and it is lost if the ship is destroyed before it is sold.
An interdiction can be submitted to, which ends it without damage, or evaded by turning directly away from the interdictor and holding full throttle.
A crime puts a fine or bounty on the Commander in that system, and Interstellar Factors Contact at a station can clear it for a fee.
The same commodity pays different prices at different markets, so a trader sells where demand is high and buys where supply is plentiful.
The missions panel lists each accepted mission with its destination and expiry, and a finished mission is handed in at the station its text names.
Materials gathered from planets, wrecks and ships are spent on engineer upgrades and on synthesis, and the inventory shows how many of each the ship can hold.
A shield cell bank, once fitted, restores a collapsed shield when it is fired.
Cargo canisters are scooped by flying slowly into them with the cargo scoop deployed, and flying too fast breaks them.
Flying through the jet cone of a neutron star or white dwarf supercharges the frame shift drive for a longer next jump, as long as the ship stays out of the star itself.
Engineers upgrade modules for materials, and each one asks for something different before taking a pilot on.
